ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, officers, individuals with significant control, and authorized signatories against domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), including immediate family members and close associates. Screening databases must include the OFAC SDN List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, and Canadian sanctions lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. FINTRAC-compliant customer identification and verification (CIV), ongoing transaction monitoring, source-of-funds verification, and enhanced risk assessment for medium-risk digital advertising media arbitrage. Sanctions and adverse media checks must be re-run at onboarding and continuously on a risk-based schedule.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries Online / OneStop Business Registry (British Columbia Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must contain only English or French alphabetic characters, numerals, or acceptable punctuation; foreign-language names may be used only when officially transliterated into English or French using standard romanization, and must include a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or 'Ulc'. Names must be distinguishable and not confusingly similar in the NUANS database, and must not include foreign script characters unless converted to a romanized equivalent acceptable to the British Columbia Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a formal reconsideration request in writing via BC Registries Online (OneStop) setting out grounds of distinction and non-confusion, with an amended name option if required. The registrar will re-evaluate the NUANS search report and the applicability of prohibited or restricted word criteria. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may either submit a fresh name reservation with up to three alternate name choices or apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 78. There is no statutory appeal tribunal; the registrar's decision is subject to common law standards of reasonableness.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are generally permissible for a British Columbia business corporation, provided the registered office is a physical street address located in British Columbia, is not a post-office box, and the virtual office provider is authorized to receive service of legal process and maintain the required corporate records. For ISIC 7310 affiliate media buying, a virtual office is acceptable; no physical storefront, trading floor, or warehousing presence is statutorily required. The company must maintain books, records, and minutes at the records office in BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection is estimated at 15% over the first 12 months for a medium-risk digital advertising entity. The likelihood increases to approximately 25% when the company engages in performance media buying with high transaction volumes and cross-border payments, as financial institutions and FINTRAC may require on-site compliance verification prior to account approval and during ongoing AML monitoring.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 56, ss. 10-13 (incorporation and notice of articles), s. 51 (registered office and records office), ss. 154-158 (directors), ss. 170-171 (officers); relevant forms adopted under B.C. Reg. 367/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Integrated Incorporation Application composed of the Notice of Articles and Incorporation Agreement filed through BC Corporate Online.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required. Shares are without par value, and the board fixes the consideration payable for each share under BCA s. 35. No escrow or minimum bank balance is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation accept subscriptions for the shares allotted to the founding shareholders, acknowledge payment or contractual consideration approved by the board, and cause the share register to be updated. RESOLVED that the registered office and registered records office be established at the street address set forth in the Notice of Articles. RESOLVED that the first directors set out in the Notice of Articles be designated as President, Secretary and Treasurer, with authority to execute banking, leasing and incorporation ancillary documents. RESOLVED that management place the corporation into the digital banking and compliance system, including the appointment of authorized signatories for ACH and wire transfer transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Corporate Structure Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, BC Corporate Online Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a mandatory search in the BC Corporate Registry to obtain a Name Search Report. If a distinctive name is required, file a Name Reservation through BC Corporate Online with a validity period of 14 days. Alternatively, proceed with a numbered company format, e.g., '1234567 B.C. Ltd.'. Confirm the authorized share structure, including the class of shares and voting entitlements, before filing.
required_dossiers: Consent or authorization from any person whose name or trademark is adopted, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to confusion or a restricted word, file a revised Name Reservation request or proceed as a numbered company by amending the Notice of Articles prior to incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Agreement and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Notice of Articles and Incorporation Agreement electronically through BC Corporate Online using a valid BCeID or government credential. Verify that the registered office and records office address are valid street addresses in British Columbia. E-signatures from all incorporators or their authorized legal representatives are accepted. Pay the registry filing fee and await statutory compliance review under the Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Consent of each first director to act
Address consent from the registered office service provider, if not the principal business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar raises a deficiency under BCA ss. 10-13, correct the worksheet and refile through the same online portal; an amended Notice of Articles may be submitted within 14 days without a fresh incorporation fee beyond the re-filing charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Set Up Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Online Repository
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation and the filed Notice of Articles in PDF format. Prepare the corporate minute book containing the certificate, articles, incorporation agreement, central securities register, and register of directors and officers. No notarization is required unless the documents are to be produced to a foreign bank or tax authority.
required_dossiers: Minute book records and corporate seal, if adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical or clerical error, apply to the registrar for correction under BCA s. 34(1), surrendering the original certificate and paying the applicable correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Resolution and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Registered Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting by paper or unanimous electronic consent. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, appoint officers, issue the founders' shares pursuant to approved subscriptions, and record the issuance in the central securities register. Execute consents to act as each officer and director. Resolution minutes must be kept at the registered records office.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Officer (Form BC-Officer)
Central securities register and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director is unavailable to sign, convene a supplementary meeting via written electronic consent to ratify appointments and substitute the officer; any defective issuance is cured by a further board resolution and share cancellation or reissue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Accreditations and Registry Compliance Backbone
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC Ministry of Finance; BC Corporate Online for annual report setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate Business Number (BN15) with the Canada Revenue Agency, including the corporate income tax account number. Determine the GST/HST registration obligation based on expected gross revenue of the affiliate media buying operation; registration becomes mandatory once taxable revenue exceeds the $30,000 threshold, although early election is recommended for input tax credits on media purchases. Update the corporate contact profile on BC Corporate Online to enable annual filings and compliance notifications.
required_dossiers: Director and beneficial owner identifiers for CRA registration
Bank account and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the BN15 application or GST/HST account, submit the Notice of Articles, the Certificate of Incorporation, and a board resolution confirming officers through the Represent a Client portal; CRA Business Tax Services usually resolves inconsistencies within 7 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable at the provincial industrial level for digital advertising arbitrage and affiliate media buying. A municipal General Business Licence may be required by the city of the registered office, for example the City of Vancouver Licensing Office. WorkSafeBC is the competent authority for occupational health and safety registration if any employees are engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal General Business Licence (where the registered office has a physical presence); no manufacturing, media production, or broadcasting permit is required for performance-based digital media buying under the ISIC 7310 scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Division, British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based quaternary service activity; no construction, extraction, discharge, or manufacturing trigger under the Environmental Management Act S.B.C. 2003, c. 53, and no Environmental Assessment Act registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no process wastewater, hazardous waste, or volatile organic compounds are generated by media buying operations. If the registered office undergoes tenant improvements, municipal building and waste management bylaws apply; no air discharge or industrial wastewater permit is required for the digital service operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a physical office, the municipality requires an occupier or business licence inspection confirming Building Code fire safety, egress, and structural load limits. WorkSafeBC clearance registration is required if any employees are physically working; for a virtual or remote-only office, no fire safety or structural load inspection is applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal corporate income tax (T2), GST/HST, and payroll; BC Ministry of Finance (Consumer Taxation Branch) — British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST); Corporations Canada — federal incorporation; BC Registry Services / OneStop — provincial incorporation. Primary portals: CRA My Business Account, Represent a Client, Business Registration Online (BRO), and BC eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the Business Corporation federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act; obtain the certificate of incorporation and corporation number, and appoint a Canadian resident director/agent if the corporation is controlled by non-residents. (2) Register with the CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts: RC0001 (corporate income tax/T2), RT0001 (GST/HST), and RP0001 (payroll if the BC affiliate employs Canadian staff). (3) Register for GST/HST immediately if the taxable supply threshold is exceeded (CAD 30,000, per the indirect taxation section); otherwise, voluntarily register to recover input tax credits and to zero-rate exported advertising/media-buying services. (4) Register for BC PST with the BC Ministry of Finance through eTaxBC and obtain a PST vendor number before selling taxable goods or services in BC. (5) file the T2 corporate income tax return within six months of the fiscal year end and remit any Part XIII dividend withholding on payments to the non-resident parent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Canadian Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and is not eligible for pass-through treatment. If Canadian-controlled and private (CCPC), the first CAD 500,000 of active business income qualifies for the small business deduction (federal 9% + BC 2%); other active income is taxed at approximately 27% combined federal/BC general corporate rates (15% federal + 12% BC). Dividends paid to the non-resident parent are subject to 25% Part XIII withholding tax, generally reduced to 5% by the Canada-United States tax treaty for a US parent owning at least 10% of the voting shares.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box classification regime. Available elections and mechanisms: (i) CCPC/small business deduction elections and associated-corporation allocation under ITA s. 256; (ii) GST/HST Quick Method election and annual/quarterly filing elections; (iii) ITA s. 250(5) deemed non-resident election to coordinate dual-resident corporation status; (iv) foreign affiliate and exempt-surplus elections under ITA s. 113 and Regulation 5907 for the Canadian shareholder; (v) competent-authority and advance-pricing-agreement procedures to prevent double taxation of cross-border media-buying service margins; (vi) compliance with the Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2 and 18.21), which operate as deduction-denial and withholding-override rules rather than elective classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Canada applies a federal value-added Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% administered by the CRA; British Columbia imposes a separate single-stage Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at 7% administered by the BC Ministry of Finance. No Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applies in BC. Digital advertising, affiliate media-buying, and lead-generation services supplied to Canadian persons are generally subject to GST and, where the service is a taxable PST service, to BC PST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: a supplier becomes a mandatory GST/HST registrant once consideration for taxable supplies made in Canada exceeds CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA small-supplier threshold). BC PST: every vendor selling taxable goods or taxable services in BC must register; an out-of-province or non-resident vendor must register for PST when its taxable BC sales exceed CAD 10,000 in the preceding 12 months, and small-supplier exemptions do not apply to PST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, and no statutory e-invoicing system at federal or provincial level. The CRA requires GST/HST registrants to file electronically (GST/HST NETFILE/XML), maintain auditable machine-readable business records for six years, and produce invoices evidencing zero-rated exports. The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) is voluntary. BC PST requires vendors to retain sales invoices and records in Canada for six years and to file periodic PST remittances through eTaxBC.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act applies to: (i) tangible personal property exported by the supplier or delivered to a carrier outside Canada within 60 days of the supply; and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person, provided the service is not in respect of real estate situated in Canada, is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, and is not supplied to a non-resident individual present in Canada. Advertising, affiliate media-buying, and lead-generation services sold by the BC affiliate to its foreign parent or foreign advertisers — where the campaigns are executed for offshore audiences — ordinarily qualify as zero-rated exported services. The supplier must hold reasonable contemporaneous evidence of the non-resident recipient status and of the export character of the supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration: Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) / Automated Export Declaration (CAED) filing for physical goods exported from Canada
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing the departure of goods from Canada within the 60-day zero-rating window (goods only)
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT / FX settlement records evidencing cross-border payment from the foreign affiliate
Commercial invoices and the executed media-buying agreement, insertion order, or affiliate contract identifying the non-resident recipient and the zero-rated supply
Non-resident status proof of the foreign counterparty (e.g., foreign certificate of incorporation, registry extract, or CRA non-resident declaration)
Digital campaign delivery and geo-targeting reports substantiating that the advertising services were directed to audiences outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess within four years of an assessment and indefinitely where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is shown; if zero-rating is overturned, the 5% GST on the supply is clawed back with compound interest. Inadequate export documentation attracts the gross-negligence penalty under Excise Tax Act s. 280 equal to 25% of the tax sought (minimum CAD 200). Willful evasion or fraudulent zero-rating/refund claims are criminal offences under ETA s. 327 and Income Tax Act s. 239, carrying substantial fines and imprisonment. Cross-border service payments between affiliated entities are also examined for transfer-pricing compliance under ITA s. 247; failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation may trigger adjustments, the 10% documentation penalty, and related Part XIII withholding reassessments. BC PST audits may separately reassess uncollected PST and impose provincial penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), established under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2; original statute 1934, operations commenced 11 March 1935), is the sole monetary authority and manager of Canada's official international reserves. It does not operate an exchange-control consent regime and does not approve individual cross-border payments. Prudential regulation of federally chartered banks rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing rule-making and supervision rest with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended. Neither the Bank of Canada nor any British Columbia provincial authority imposes prior authorization for FX transactions or capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the Canadian dollar (CAD, ISO 4217). The federal Foreign Exchange Control Act was terminated in 1952 and no successor exchange-control statute has been enacted, so there are no surrender requirements, dual exchange rates, advance import deposits, FX allocation quotas, or administrative licensing for external payments or profit repatriation. For an ISIC 7310/NAICS 541810 affiliate media buying corporation, all commercial payments to foreign publishers, DSPs, ad networks, and affiliate partners may be freely remitted in any convertible currency. Profit-remittance frictions are exclusively tax-based: Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) imposes a statutory 25% withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents, reduced under tax treaties - for example, the Canada-US Income Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 2007 Protocol) applies a 5% rate for a US corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the voting stock, and 15% for most other US residents; the Canada-UK Convention provides analogous relief. Such withholding is a CRA tax-collection mechanism, not an FX control. The CAD trades in a free float; the Bank of Canada does not restrict purchases of foreign currency for business or investment purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for the repatriation, deposit, or conversion of export proceeds or cross-border service revenue, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio for foreign currency received by a Canadian business corporation. A British Columbia affiliate media buying entity may retain 100% of USD, EUR, GBP, and other foreign currency receipts in foreign currency accounts at Canadian banks indefinitely, convert to CAD at its own election, or pledge such balances as collateral without central bank approval. The only applicable compliance duties are: (i) FINTRAC cross-border wire transfer reporting (CBWTR) by the financial institution for international wires of CAD 10,000 or more; (ii) FINTRAC large cash transaction reporting (LCTR) for cash transactions of CAD 10,000 or more; (iii) annual CRA tax filing translated into CAD at the Bank of Canada spot rate or a rate that reasonably reflects market value under subsection 261(2) of the Income Tax Act; and (iv) the requirement not to structure transactions to evade reporting thresholds. There are no export surrender ratios, forced conversion timelines, or central bank ledger controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (annual corporate return under the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 56)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing is due within two months after each anniversary of the corporation's date of incorporation; a newly incorporated BC company files its first annual report within two months after its first incorporation anniversary. The deadline is anchored to the incorporation anniversary, not to the fiscal year-end. Online filing via BC Registries is subject to a statutory fee of CAD 61.75.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company in default of the annual report is not in good standing and may receive a default notice from the Registrar; after failure to file annual reports for at least two consecutive years and failure to remedy the statutory notice, the Registrar may administratively strike the company off the register and the company is dissolved. Reinstatement requires a court restoration order and payment of all outstanding annual report fees and filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and accompanying financial statements (CRA annual corporate filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The T2 return must be filed within six months after the end of the corporation's taxation/fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following year. The balance of tax payable is due on the balance-due day, generally within two months after fiscal year-end for non-CCPC corporations and within three months after fiscal year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month up to a maximum of 12 months; a repeated failure penalty of 10% may apply; daily prescribed-rate interest accrues on unpaid amounts; wilful non-filing or false statements may trigger gross-negligence penalties and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return and instalment reconciliation where the corporation files annually under the Excise Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an approved annual GST/HST filer, the annual return is due within three months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. Monthly and quarterly filers remit on their normal period deadlines and are not required to file an additional annual reconciliation unless CRA requests one.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual GST/HST return attracts a penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; daily interest is charged on arrears; continued non-filing may trigger CRA audit and collection enforcement including seizure of assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: British Columbia does not impose a revenue or asset threshold that automatically requires an independent audit for a private business corporation. Under the Business Corporations Act, a BC company must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless all voting shareholders unanimously pass a resolution waiving the audit appointment, or unless the company is a reporting issuer under provincial securities law, in which case an auditor is mandatory. Lending agreements, commercial contracts, or affiliated group requirements may also contractually require audited financial statements for the media-buying affiliate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian generally accepted accounting principles (Canadian GAAP): IFRS as set out in CPA Canada Handbook Part I applies to publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is the usual framework for a private BC affiliate media-buying corporation. The financial statements submitted with the CRA T2 return must be prepared using Canadian GAAP or another acceptable accounting framework prescribed by CRA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act, a BC company must maintain a current transparency register of each significant individual holding 25% or more of the voting shares or exercising control in fact over the company. The transparency register is not filed separately with the Registrar on an annual basis; it must be kept at the records office in British Columbia and produced to the Registrar of Companies, law enforcement, tax authorities, or other lawful requesters on demand. The BC annual report confirms only the registered office and current directors and contains no separate shareholder or UBO attestation. Every allotment and transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members as it occurs, and directors are required to ensure the transparency register and Register of Members are accurate as of each fiscal year-end. Knowingly maintaining false particulars or failing to keep the required registers is an offence subject to fines and imprisonment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including share allotment and transfer history)
